common_confusions: BC-MIS-10001 (a statement about the terms taken to settle the total)
BC-SKL-10011 (limit of the general term, computed for the series rather than the sequence)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10001 (a series is presented and the prompt asks what the terms do, so the answer has to name which object it describes)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response evaluates the limit of a sub n as n increases without bound, reports that single number as the limit of the sequence, and says the sequence converges to it, or reports divergence when no finite limit exists; the sentence names the sequence rather than the series, and the ratio of leading behaviours in n is handled correctly in both the sigma form and the listed-terms form. BC-ERR-10001 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit of a sub n is computed correctly but the closing sentence attaches the number to the series rather than to the sequence, which is BC-ERR-10001, the object being described is left unnamed, or convergence is asserted with no limit value supplied.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The response cannot evaluate a limit of a ratio of polynomial or exponential expressions in n at all, so nothing about the sequence is produced: that is BC-PRQ-10004, and the limit technique of BC-SKL-01015 rather than sequence language.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the sequence as a list of terms with its own limit) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (limits of ratios in the index) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a sequence defined by a formula in n, evaluate the limit of the terms as n increases without bound and report convergence to that value or divergence.
skills.description_plain: Decide whether the terms of a sequence approach a single number and say which number.
skills.name: Determine whether a sequence converges and find its limit

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10002 (the total of the first few terms read as the value of the series)
BC-SKL-10003 (the limit of S sub n, which is a different request)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10002 (asks for the value of the series, so a partial sum offered as the answer is visible immediately)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response adds exactly the first n terms of the series, presents S sub n either as a number for a stated n or as an expression in n, and labels it a partial sum rather than the value of the series; the index range read off the sigma matches the terms written, with the lower index respected.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The arithmetic of the first n terms is right but the total is offered as the value of the infinite series, which is BC-ERR-10002, or the count of terms is off by one because the lower index on the sigma was read as one when it is zero.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Sigma notation itself is not decoded, so the terms summed do not match the general term: that is BC-PRQ-06006 and BC-PRQ-10008, not a partial-sum gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10002 (partial sum against limit of partial sums) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06006 (summation notation) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series in sigma or expanded form, write the sum of its first n terms, either as a numerical value for a stated n or as an expression in n.
skills.description_plain: Add the first n terms and report the total as a function of n.
skills.name: Compute the nth partial sum of a series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10002 (a partial sum read as the value of the series)
BC-SKL-10002 (computing S sub n without the cancellation structure)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10002 (a value is requested and the cancellation plus limit is the only route to it)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response splits the general term into a difference of consecutive expressions, writes S sub n with the interior terms cancelled so that only the surviving first and last pieces remain, and takes the limit of that remainder to report the sum; the surviving boundary terms match the lower index of the sigma.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The split into a difference is correct and the cancellation leaves the wrong boundary terms, or the cancelled form is produced and the limit is never taken so a partial sum is reported as the value, which is BC-ERR-10002.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The difference of consecutive expressions cannot be lined up because the index cannot be shifted, which is BC-PRQ-10003, or the general term is misread from the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10002 (the value as a limit of partial sums) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10003 (index shifting) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series whose terms split into a difference of consecutive expressions, write S sub n with the interior cancellation carried out and evaluate its limit.
skills.description_plain: Cancel the interior terms of the running total and take the limit of what is left.
skills.name: Evaluate a telescoping series through its partial sums

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10001 (a claim about one object taken to settle the other)
BC-SKL-10001 (the sequence limit)
BC-SKL-10011 (the general term limit inside a series question)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10001 (several series can appear in one part, so the verdict has to name its subject)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states which of the two objects the prompt names, the list of terms a sub n or the sum of those terms, attaches the convergence question to that object, and names it explicitly in the verdict sentence when more than one series is on the page. BC-ERR-10001 and BC-ERR-10003 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The right object is identified in the work and the closing sentence still says the series when the sequence was meant, which is BC-ERR-10001, or a verdict is stated with no referent where several series appear in the part, which is BC-ERR-10003.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Function notation itself is not read, so a sub n and the sigma expression are not distinguished as written: that is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a sequence and series distinction.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10001 (terms against accumulated total) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (function and index notation) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a prompt naming a sequence of terms and a series built from them, identify which convergence question is being asked and which limit answers it.
skills.description_plain: Say which object is being asked about, the list of terms or their total.
skills.name: Distinguish a sequence from its associated series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10003 (the geometric closed form used whenever terms shrink)
BC-MIS-10004 (the first term assumed to sit at index zero)
BC-SKL-10018 (p-series form mistaken for geometric form)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the closed form is requested, so a and r have to be named before anything else)
BC-QA-10001 (test selection turns on whether the ratio is constant)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response divides consecutive terms, shows the quotient is the same constant for every index, and reports both the first term as the series is actually written and that common ratio; the ratio equals the quotient of consecutive terms rather than a coefficient or an exponent read off the general term. BC-ERR-10004 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A constant ratio is recognised and the number named as r is the base of the power or the leading coefficient rather than the quotient of consecutive terms, which is BC-ERR-10004, or r is correct and the first term is taken from the index zero position when the sigma starts elsewhere.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Consecutive terms cannot be produced from the sigma at all, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the quotient is formed and mis-simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10003 (a constant quotient as what makes a series geometric) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10005 (computing a common ratio) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series in expanded or sigma form, divide consecutive terms, confirm the quotient is constant, and report the first term of the series as written together with the common ratio.
skills.description_plain: Check that consecutive terms share a constant quotient and name a and r.
skills.name: Identify a series as geometric and state its first term and ratio

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10003 (decreasing terms taken as licence for the closed form)
BC-SKL-10019 (the p-series threshold on the exponent applied to a ratio)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the sum is asked for, so the condition on r is the step that licenses it)
BC-QA-10020 (a geometric ratio argument is an accepted reason for convergence at a stated input)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states the criterion that a geometric series converges when the absolute value of r is less than one and diverges otherwise, applies it to the r found, and gives the verdict before any sum is written. BC-ERR-10005 is absent, so no finite value is attached to a series with absolute value of r at least one.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The criterion is stated and the absolute value bars are dropped when r is negative, so the comparison is made on the signed ratio, or the closed form is written first and the size of r is checked afterwards, leaving BC-ERR-10005 in reach.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The inequality on the absolute value of r cannot be resolved into a condition on the variable, which is BC-PRQ-10001 rather than a geometric criterion gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10003 (what the size of the ratio controls) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10001 (absolute value inequalities) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a geometric series, state that it converges when the absolute value of the common ratio is less than one and diverges otherwise, and apply that condition to the ratio found.
skills.description_plain: Decide convergence by comparing the size of the ratio with one.
skills.name: Apply the convergence condition for a geometric series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10004 (the sum formula read as requiring the index zero term)
BC-MIS-10002 (a partial sum offered as the value)
BC-SKL-10009 (the shifted-index case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the closed form is the scored object)
BC-QA-10002 (a value is requested and a partial sum earns nothing)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response forms the quotient of the first term as written over one minus r and reports the value, leaving it unsimplified where the prompt supplies the closed form; the numerator is the term the series actually begins with and the denominator carries one minus the ratio rather than one plus it.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The pair a and r is correct and the sum is built from the index zero term although the sigma begins elsewhere, which is BC-ERR-10006, or the first several terms are added instead of the closed form being applied, which is BC-ERR-10002.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The common ratio cannot be extracted from the terms, which is BC-PRQ-10005; the sum formula is then applied to numbers that were never a and r.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10004 (which term the formula calls a) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10005 (ratio extraction) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a convergent geometric series with first term a and ratio r, report the sum as a divided by one minus r.
skills.description_plain: Divide the first term by one minus the ratio.
skills.name: Compute the sum of a convergent geometric series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10004 (the first term assumed to be the index zero term)
BC-SKL-10008 (the standard-form sum)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the closed form is requested from a sigma whose lower index is not zero)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response reads the lower index on the sigma, writes out the term produced by that index, and uses it as a in the quotient a over one minus r, or re-indexes the sum to start at zero and carries the resulting factor; the reported value matches the series as printed. BC-ERR-10006 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The ratio is right and a is taken from the index zero position, which is BC-ERR-10006, or the re-indexing route is chosen and the compensating power of r is dropped, so the value is off by exactly one factor of r.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The index cannot be shifted or the general term cannot be evaluated at the printed lower index, which is BC-PRQ-10003 with BC-PRQ-10008 rather than a geometric sum gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10004 (the first term as the one the series begins with) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10003 (re-indexing a sum) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a geometric series whose sigma notation starts at an index other than zero, identify the first term as written and apply the sum formula, or re-index the series before summing.
skills.description_plain: Take the first term as the one the series actually starts with, not the n equals zero term.
skills.name: Sum a geometric series whose index does not start at zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10003 (closed form used without checking the size of the ratio)
BC-MIS-10023 (the interior taken as the complete convergence answer)
BC-SKL-10072 (closed form recognition for a numerical power series)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the closed form is scored with the condition on the ratio attached)
BC-QA-10020 (the ratio argument decides convergence at a stated input)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response treats an expression in x as the common ratio, writes the closed form with that expression in the denominator, and records the inequality on the absolute value of the ratio that makes the closed form valid, converting it into a condition on x. BC-ERR-10005 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The closed form in x is written and the validity inequality is omitted, so the representation is claimed for every x, which is BC-ERR-10005, or the inequality is written in the ratio and never solved for x.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The absolute value inequality in the ratio cannot be turned into an interval in x, which is BC-PRQ-10001, or the constant quotient is not identified, which is BC-PRQ-10005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10003 (validity of a geometric closed form) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10001 (absolute value inequalities in x) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a power series that is geometric in x, identify the first term and the ratio as expressions in x, write the closed form, and state the inequality on the ratio that makes it valid.
skills.description_plain: Treat the expression in x as the ratio, sum it, and record where the sum is valid.
skills.name: Sum a geometric series whose ratio contains the variable

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10005 (the nth term test read as working in both directions)
BC-SKL-10001 (the same limit computed as a statement about a sequence)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the test computation is scored separately from the verdict)
BC-QA-10001 (the form of a sub n drives the choice of test)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response extracts a sub n from the sigma, including any alternating factor, and evaluates the limit of a sub n as n increases without bound, with the limit symbol present and the ratio of like degrees in n resolved to the quotient of leading coefficients rather than to zero. BC-ERR-10007 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The general term is extracted correctly and the limit value is wrong, typically a ratio of equal degrees reported as zero, which is BC-ERR-10007, so any verdict resting on it carries no reasoning credit.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be read out of the sigma at all, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the limit of the ratio in n is the blocker, which is BC-PRQ-10004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the general term as the object of the limit) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (limits of ratios in n) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series in sigma form, extract the general term and evaluate its limit as n increases without bound.
skills.description_plain: Take the limit of a sub n as the index grows.
skills.name: Evaluate the limit of the general term of a series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10006 (a one way test read as reversible)
BC-SKL-10013 (the inconclusive branch of the same test)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (one point for the right object and one for the verdict with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response shows the limit of a sub n is nonzero or fails to exist, names the nth term test, and concludes that the series diverges, with the series named in the conclusion; the divergence claim is tied to the computed limit rather than asserted. BC-ERR-10009 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The nonzero limit is computed and the test is not named, or the test is named and the limit that licenses it is never displayed, which is BC-ERR-10009, so the justification point is not supported.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit of a sub n cannot be evaluated, so no divergence claim can be grounded: that is BC-PRQ-10004 rather than a gap in the nth term test.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10006 (the one way direction of the nth term test) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (evaluating the limit of a sub n) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a general term whose limit is nonzero or does not exist, name the nth term test and conclude that the series diverges.
skills.description_plain: State divergence because the terms do not shrink to zero.
skills.name: Conclude divergence when the general term does not approach zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10007 (hypotheses and setup treated as ceremony around a named test)
BC-SKL-06067 (improper integral setup in the integration unit)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10005 (the improper integral is a separate scored step from the conditions and the evaluation)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the integral of f of x with the lower limit equal to the index the series starts at and an upper limit carried as a variable inside limit notation; the integrand matches a sub n with the index replaced by the continuous variable. BC-ERR-10012 and BC-ERR-10011 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integrand is correct and the lower limit is one when the sigma starts elsewhere, which is BC-ERR-10012, or the integral is opened with the infinity symbol in place of limit notation, which is BC-ERR-10011; a correct subsequent limit keeps the evaluation point in reach.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The switch from the index n to a bound continuous variable is not made, which is BC-PRQ-06013, or f of x cannot be written from a sub n at all, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the correspondence between the series and the integral) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06013 (bound variables) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series of terms f of n, write the corresponding improper integral with the correct lower limit and with limit notation for the upper limit.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral of f from the starting index to infinity as a limit.
skills.name: Set up the improper integral that matches the series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10008 (the integral test read as an evaluation rather than a comparison)
BC-MIS-10002 (a number reported as the series value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10005 (the conclusion is the step the conditions and the integral were built for)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the series converges because the matching improper integral converges, or diverges because the integral diverges, names which series the verdict is about, and makes no claim that the integral's value is the sum. BC-ERR-10013 and BC-ERR-10003 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is evaluated to a finite number and that number is reported as the sum of the series, which is BC-ERR-10013, or the verdict is correct and no series is named where several appear in the part, which is BC-ERR-10003.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The correspondence between f of n and a sub n is not held, so the conclusion is drawn about the wrong object, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10008 (what the integral test transfers and what it does not) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (matching f of n to a sub n) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a convergent or divergent improper integral and the verified conditions, conclude that the series converges or diverges by the integral test, naming the series.
skills.description_plain: Report that the series behaves as the integral does, without claiming the two have the same value.
skills.name: Conclude convergence or divergence of the series from the integral

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10009 (the convergence boundary placed away from p equal to one)
BC-SKL-10006 (geometric form, where the index sits in the exponent instead of the base)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the named test follows directly from the family)
BC-QA-10001 (family recognition is the cue for test choice)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names the family the series belongs to, harmonic, alternating harmonic, or p-series with the value of p stated, after rewriting any root or negative exponent as a single exponent on n; a series with a constant ratio or a factorial is correctly excluded from these families. BC-ERR-10014 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The family is named and the exponent is read off wrongly after a root is converted, so a p at most one is labelled convergent, which is BC-ERR-10014, or the alternating harmonic series is classified as harmonic with the sign factor ignored.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The root or reciprocal form cannot be converted to a power of n at all, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the alternating factor is not read out of the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10009 (what defines a p-series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (converting roots to exponents) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series, identify it as the harmonic series, the alternating harmonic series, a p-series with a stated p, or none of these.
skills.description_plain: Name which standard family a series belongs to.
skills.name: Classify a series as harmonic, alternating harmonic, or p-series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10009 (the threshold placed elsewhere than at one)
BC-MIS-10005 (terms tending to zero taken as sufficient)
BC-SKL-10007 (the geometric condition on the ratio)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the verdict and its reason are scored together)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response compares the exponent p with one, states that the p-series converges when p is greater than one and diverges when p is at most one, and applies that to the exponent actually present, including the case p equal to one. BC-ERR-10014 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The criterion is stated with the boundary at one and the strict case is mishandled, so p equal to one is called convergent, or the criterion is applied to a series that is not a p-series.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The exponent is misread because a radical or a reciprocal was not converted, which is BC-PRQ-06002 rather than a gap in the criterion itself.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10009 (the p-series threshold) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (reading the exponent) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a p-series, state that it converges when p is greater than one and diverges when p is at most one, and apply that to the exponent present.
skills.description_plain: Compare the exponent with one and state convergence or divergence.
skills.name: Apply the p-series criterion

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10005 (terms going to zero read as convergence, with the harmonic series as the refutation)
BC-SKL-10018 (family classification)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10015 (the comparison to the harmonic series carries the endpoint part)
BC-QA-10004 (a named reference series supplies the reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states without rederivation that the harmonic series diverges and that the alternating harmonic series converges, and uses one of them as a named reference series in a comparison or as the counterexample to a limit of zero implying convergence. BC-ERR-10014 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two behaviours are recalled and swapped, or the harmonic series is cited correctly and the sign factor is ignored when the alternating one is the series in hand.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term one over n is not recognised from the printed form, which is BC-PRQ-06005, so no standard series can be named.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10005 (the harmonic series as the standing counterexample) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (recognising one over n) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Reproduce, without rederivation, that the harmonic series diverges and that the alternating harmonic series converges, and use either as a reference series in a comparison.
skills.description_plain: State that the harmonic series diverges and the alternating harmonic series converges.
skills.name: Recall the behaviour of the harmonic and alternating harmonic series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10007 (the name of the test taken as the argument)
BC-MIS-10014 (a ratio limit of one read as a result)
BC-SKL-10022 (choosing the comparison series once comparison is chosen)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10001 (the choice is free, so the verdict rests on the conditions of whatever test is chosen)
BC-QA-10015 (the two endpoint series often need different tests)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names a test whose hypotheses this series meets and ties the choice to a visible feature of a sub n, a constant quotient for the geometric test, a factorial or a power of n for the ratio test, a rational expression for comparison or limit comparison against a p-series, a sign changing factor for the alternating series test, or a positive decreasing continuous f for the integral test, and the conditions are verified rather than asserted. BC-ERR-10009 and BC-ERR-10015 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A test that does fit is named and its conditions are never established, which is BC-ERR-10009, or a comparison is aimed at an alternating series or the alternating series test at a series of positive terms, which is BC-ERR-10015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be read out of the sigma, so no form cue is available, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or a constant quotient is not recognised, which is BC-PRQ-10005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10007 (matching hypotheses to the series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (reading the general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series, name a test whose hypotheses the series meets, using cues such as a constant ratio for the geometric test, a factorial or a power of n for the ratio test, a rational expression for comparison or limit comparison to a p-series, an alternating factor for the alternating series test, and a positive decreasing continuous function for the integral test.
skills.description_plain: Choose the test that matches the shape of the terms before computing anything.
skills.name: Select an appropriate convergence test from the form of the general term

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10009 (the p-series criterion applied to series that are not p-series)
BC-SKL-10025 (limit comparison, which tolerates a mismatch in constant factors)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the comparison series is the object the test is run on)
BC-QA-10015 (the endpoint series is matched against a standard reference)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names an explicit comparison series b sub n, a geometric series or a p-series, whose terms match the dominant behaviour of a sub n for large n, states it in sigma or general term form, and restricts the comparison to nonnegative terms. BC-ERR-10015 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A comparison series is named and its exponent or ratio does not match the dominant behaviour, so the inequality that follows cannot be established, or a comparison is attempted on a series whose terms change sign, which is BC-ERR-10015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The dominant behaviour cannot be identified because the ratio of powers in n is not simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10004, or the exponent after a root conversion is wrong, which is BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (dominant behaviour of terms for large n) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (ratios of powers in n) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series with nonnegative terms, select a geometric series or p-series whose terms agree with the dominant behaviour of a sub n for large n, and state the comparison series explicitly.
skills.description_plain: Pick a standard series whose terms match the dominant behaviour.
skills.name: Choose a comparison series for a given series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10010 (the direction of the inequality untied from the conclusion)
BC-SKL-10023 (establishing the inequality, the step before this one)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the verdict with a reason is the scored object)
BC-QA-10015 (the endpoint verdict rests on the comparison)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response combines the stated inequality with the known behaviour of b sub n into the verdict the direct comparison test supports, convergence when the larger series converges and divergence when the smaller one diverges, and names which series the verdict is about. BC-ERR-10016 and BC-ERR-10003 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The inequality and the reference behaviour are both correct and the conclusion drawn is the one the direction does not support, which is BC-ERR-10016, or the verdict is right and no series is identified where several appear, which is BC-ERR-10003.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The behaviour of the comparison series is not known, so nothing can be transferred: that is a p-series or geometric recall gap, BC-SKL-10019 or BC-SKL-10007, rather than a comparison gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10010 (what each direction of comparison implies) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10019 (behaviour of the reference p-series) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

skills.name: Conclude convergence or divergence by direct comparison

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10011 (the ratio test threshold of one carried into the limit comparison)
BC-SKL-10031 (the ratio of consecutive terms, a different quotient)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10006 (the setup point turns on limit notation and the reciprocal is accepted)
BC-QA-10015 (limit comparison applied at an endpoint)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response forms the quotient of a sub n by b sub n, or its reciprocal, and writes it inside limit notation as n increases without bound, with absolute value bars present when the claim concerns absolute convergence. BC-ERR-10017 and BC-ERR-10018 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The quotient is formed correctly and the limit symbol is omitted, so a value is asserted as the index grows, which is BC-ERR-10017, or the quotient is run on signed terms while absolute convergence is the claim, which is BC-ERR-10018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The quotient of powers with the same base cannot be simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10007, or the limit of the resulting ratio cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10011 (which quotient the limit comparison takes) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10007 (simplifying ratios of powers) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series and a chosen comparison series, write the limit as n increases without bound of a sub n divided by b sub n, or its reciprocal, with limit notation present.
skills.description_plain: Write the limit of the quotient of the two general terms.
skills.name: Set up the limit comparison ratio with limit notation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10012 (the alternating factor treated as the whole of the test)
BC-SKL-10034 (forming the absolute value series for a different purpose)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the shape of the series decides which test may be named)
BC-QA-10015 (a negative endpoint produces the alternating factor)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response points to the factor that changes the sign from term to term, a power of negative one or a cosine of n pi, and writes the sequence of absolute values of the terms as a separate object with the sign factor stripped. BC-ERR-10015 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The alternating factor is spotted and the absolute values are never written, so the size conditions have nothing to be checked on, or a series of positive terms is treated as alternating because a negative sign appears in a constant, which is BC-ERR-10015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sign factor cannot be read out of the sigma notation, which is BC-PRQ-10008 rather than an alternating series gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10012 (what the alternating factor alone establishes) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (reading an alternating factor) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series in sigma or expanded form, identify the factor that alternates the sign and write the sequence of absolute values of the terms.
skills.description_plain: Spot the factor that flips the sign from term to term.
skills.name: Recognise a series as alternating

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10013 (the two conditions collapsed into one)
BC-SKL-10029 (the limit condition, the other half of the test)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the conditions carry the reason point)
BC-QA-10008 (the bound is licensed only once both conditions are stated)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response shows that the absolute values of the terms form a decreasing sequence from the starting index onward, by an explicit inequality between consecutive absolute values or by the sign of the derivative of the matching function, and states the decrease as one of the two alternating series conditions. BC-ERR-10020 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The decrease is asserted from the first few terms with no argument that it continues for every index, or the decrease is shown and the limit condition is never stated, which is BC-ERR-10020 and the collapse described in BC-MIS-10013.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The comparison between consecutive absolute values cannot be resolved because the ratio in n is not handled, which is BC-PRQ-10004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10013 (the two separate requirements of the alternating series test) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (comparing consecutive terms) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an alternating series, show that the absolute values of the terms form a decreasing sequence from the starting index onward.
skills.description_plain: Check that each term is smaller in size than the one before it.
skills.name: Verify that the terms decrease in absolute value

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10013 (one condition stated for two)
BC-MIS-10005 (a limit of zero read as sufficient for convergence)
BC-SKL-10013 (the inconclusive nth term test case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the reason point requires both conditions)
BC-QA-10008 (the error bound rests on the same two conditions)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response evaluates the limit of the absolute values of the terms and states that it is zero, presenting it as the second alternating series condition alongside the decrease rather than as a convergence argument in itself. BC-ERR-10020 and BC-ERR-10008 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit of zero is produced and the decrease condition is omitted, which is BC-ERR-10020, or the zero limit alone is offered as the reason the series converges, which is BC-ERR-10008.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit of the absolute value expression in n cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10005 (what a zero limit settles on its own) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (limits of the absolute terms) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an alternating series, evaluate the limit of the absolute values of the terms and confirm it is zero.
skills.description_plain: Check that the size of the terms has limit zero.
skills.name: Verify that the terms tend to zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10012 (the alternating factor taken as the whole test)
BC-MIS-10007 (the test name treated as the argument)
BC-SKL-10058 (the same test applied at an endpoint)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (a conclusion with no supporting condition earns the first point only)
BC-QA-10015 (an alternating endpoint series needs both conditions stated)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names the alternating series test, states both that the terms alternate in sign with absolute values decreasing and that those absolute values have limit zero, and concludes convergence for the named series. BC-ERR-10020 and BC-ERR-10009 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One of the two conditions is stated and the other is left out while the verdict is given, which is BC-ERR-10020, or the test is named with no condition attached at all, which is BC-ERR-10009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The terms cannot be read as a signed sequence in n, which is BC-PRQ-06005, so neither condition can be stated.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10012 (the full hypothesis set of the alternating series test) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading the signed general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an alternating series whose terms decrease in absolute value to zero, state both conditions and conclude convergence by the alternating series test.
skills.description_plain: Name the test and state that the terms decrease in magnitude to zero.
skills.name: Conclude convergence by the alternating series test with both conditions stated

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10014 (a ratio limit of one treated as a result)
BC-SKL-10025 (the limit comparison quotient of two different series)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10013 (the ratio is the first of five points and is banked once earned)
BC-QA-10014 (the limit point requires the ratio point first)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the absolute value of a sub n plus one over a sub n with n plus one substituted in every place the index occurs, including inside factorials and exponents such as two n plus three where two n plus one stood, and keeps the absolute value bars. BC-ERR-10021 and BC-ERR-10022 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution is made in some positions and not others, most visibly in an exponent, which is BC-ERR-10021 and keeps the early points while blocking the final interval, or the bars are dropped, which is BC-ERR-10022.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A ratio of factorials cannot be simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10002, or a quotient of powers with the same base cannot be reduced, which is BC-PRQ-10007.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (what the ratio test compares) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (factorial ratios) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series, write the quotient of the term with index n plus one by the term with index n, taking absolute values and substituting n plus one everywhere the index appears.
skills.description_plain: Write the next term over the current term, in absolute value.
skills.name: Set up the ratio of consecutive terms of a series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10014 (a limit of one read as a result rather than as a failure of the test)
BC-SKL-10026 (the limit comparison criterion, where one is not a threshold)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the verdict must rest on the computed limit)
BC-QA-10001 (the ratio test may be chosen where its limit decides nothing)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response reads the ratio limit against one and states absolute convergence when it is below one, divergence when it is above one, and that the test yields nothing when it equals one, naming the inconclusive case explicitly rather than defaulting to a verdict. BC-ERR-10009 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two decisive cases are handled and a limit of exactly one is converted into a verdict, or the correct verdict is stated with the ratio limit never displayed, which is BC-ERR-10009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The inequality involving the absolute value of the limit cannot be resolved, which is BC-PRQ-10001 rather than a gap in the criterion.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10014 (the inconclusive case of the ratio test) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10001 (absolute value inequalities) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the value of the ratio limit, state that the series converges absolutely when the limit is less than one, diverges when it is greater than one, and that the test is inconclusive when it equals one.
skills.description_plain: Compare the limit with one and state convergence, divergence, or no conclusion.
skills.name: Conclude from the value of the ratio limit, including the inconclusive case

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10015 (absolute and conditional used as interchangeable labels)
BC-SKL-10027 (recognising the alternating factor, the step before)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10007 (the explanation point requires the absolute value bars to be visible)
BC-QA-10006 (limit comparison is the usual vehicle on the absolute value series)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the series of absolute values of the terms with the sign factor removed, applies a named test to that series, and reports convergence or divergence of the absolute value series as a claim separate from any claim about the signed series; absolute value bars appear in the work. BC-ERR-10018 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A test is run and it is run on the signed terms while the claim made is about absolute convergence, which is BC-ERR-10018, or the absolute value series is written and the verdict never states which of the two series it concerns.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The alternating factor cannot be identified and removed from the general term, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10015 (two distinct series, two distinct tests) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (stripping the alternating factor) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series with mixed signs, write the series of absolute values and apply an appropriate test to it, reporting convergence or divergence of that series.
skills.description_plain: Strip the signs and decide whether that series converges.
skills.name: Test the series of absolute values

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10015 (the two labels treated as one)
BC-MIS-10016 (the two classifications ordered on a single scale)
BC-SKL-10035 (the absolute case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10007 (the classification requires both verdicts and a named series)
BC-QA-10015 (a conditionally convergent endpoint series is the usual setting)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response reports two findings, that the signed series converges and that the series of absolute values diverges, and gives the label conditionally convergent with both findings as the reason. BC-ERR-10023 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both tests are run and the label attached reverses them, which is BC-ERR-10023, or only one of the two findings is produced and the label is written as though both had been established.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: One of the two tests cannot be carried out on its series, so only one verdict exists: that points at BC-SKL-10034 or BC-SKL-10030 rather than at the classification.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10016 (conditional and absolute as exclusive, not graded) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10034 (testing the absolute value series) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that a series converges and that the series of absolute values diverges, state that the series converges conditionally and give both findings as the reason.
skills.description_plain: Say the series converges but its absolute value series does not.
skills.name: Classify a series as conditionally convergent

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10016 (the two classifications placed on one scale)
BC-SKL-10035 (labelling, as against drawing the implication)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10007 (the implication is what links the two series in the classification)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response moves from convergence of the series of absolute values to convergence of the signed series and cites that absolute convergence implies convergence as the warrant, without rerunning a test on the signed series. BC-ERR-10023 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The implication is used and the resulting series is then labelled conditionally convergent, which is BC-ERR-10023, or the implication is asserted in the reverse direction, from convergence of the signed series to absolute convergence.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Convergence of the absolute value series was never established, so the implication has no antecedent: that is BC-SKL-10034.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10016 (the one way implication between the two series) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10034 (establishing the antecedent) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that the series of absolute values converges, conclude that the original series converges, citing that absolute convergence implies convergence.
skills.description_plain: Move from convergence of the absolute value series to convergence of the series itself.
skills.name: Use absolute convergence to conclude convergence

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10016 (rearrangement assumed safe for any convergent series)
BC-SKL-10036 (the conditional case, where the property fails)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10007 (the classification determines whether the property may be invoked)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that regrouping or rearranging the terms of an absolutely convergent series leaves its value unchanged, and confines that claim to the absolutely convergent case rather than extending it to a conditionally convergent series such as the alternating harmonic series. BC-ERR-10023 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The invariance is stated correctly and then applied to a series only shown to converge, without the absolute value series having been tested, so the hypothesis of the statement is not in hand.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The series has not been classified at all, so there is no basis on which to invoke the property: that is BC-SKL-10035 rather than a rearrangement gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10016 (what absolute convergence buys beyond convergence) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10035 (classifying before invoking) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10018 (the bounding expression treated as the exact error)
BC-SKL-10040 (identifying the term, the step before the substitution)

adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct omitted term is identified and the index or the centre is substituted in place of the input, which is BC-ERR-10025, or the power in the term is evaluated with an arithmetic slip while the setup stands.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The power or factorial in the term cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the term cannot be read from the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10018 (bound against exact error) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (evaluating the power) for the procedural case

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10019 (values attached directly to the powers)
BC-SKL-10044 (the same assembly from values obtained by differentiating)

BC-ERR-10031 and BC-ERR-10029 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The values are located in the table and one is paired with the power of a different order, which is BC-ERR-10031, or every value is placed correctly with the factorial denominators missing, which is BC-ERR-10029.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The table rows cannot be read as orders of derivative at a point, which is BC-PRQ-06005, or the factorials cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10019 (coefficient as value over factorial) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-02008 (reading values from a table) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-10011
skills.description_formal: Given a table listing f and its derivatives at a point, select the entries for the required orders and assemble the Taylor polynomial of the stated degree about that point.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested degree not binding)
BC-MIS-10021 (the series treated as valid at every input)
BC-SKL-10065 (multiplying a known series by an expression)

BC-ERR-10028 and BC-ERR-10030 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The route through the known series is taken and terms beyond the requested degree or an ellipsis are carried along, which is BC-ERR-10030, or the defining relation is differentiated with a factor dropped, which is BC-ERR-10028, or a coefficient of the right shape appears with no supporting work.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The defining relation cannot be read as connecting the two functions, which is BC-PRQ-06005, or the factorials cannot be handled, which is BC-PRQ-10002.

skills.description_formal: Given a function defined from another by a product, a derivative, or an antiderivative, produce the requested Taylor polynomial by operating on a known series or by differentiating the defining relation.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (the representation assumed valid at every input)

BC-QA-10009 (the approximation is what the error bound is written about)

adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution is carried out and the result is presented as the exact value of the function, or extra terms past the requested degree are included before evaluating, which is BC-ERR-10030.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The polynomial cannot be evaluated at the input because function notation and substitution are the blocker, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10021 (approximation against exact value) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (evaluating the polynomial) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10018 (the bound written as the exact error)
BC-SKL-10042 (the alternating series bound, which uses a term rather than a derivative)

BC-ERR-10032 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The bound is assembled with two of the three parts correct, most often the power of x minus a carrying n instead of n plus one, or the factorial being n factorial, which is BC-ERR-10032 and takes the comparison point with it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorial cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10002, or the power of the displacement cannot be formed, which is BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the structure of the Lagrange remainder) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (the factorial denominator) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the degree, the centre, the input, and a bound on the next derivative, write the error bound as that bound multiplied by the absolute value of the difference raised to the n plus first power divided by n plus one factorial.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10018 (bound treated as exact error)
BC-SKL-10042 (the alternating series comparison against a tolerance)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10009 (the second point is showing the error is at most the tolerance)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response evaluates the assembled Lagrange bound to a number and presents the inequality that the absolute error is at most that number and that the number is at most the stated tolerance, using inequality symbols throughout. BC-ERR-10026 and BC-ERR-10027 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The bound is assembled correctly and the relation to the error is written with an equals sign, which is BC-ERR-10026, or the number is produced and never compared with the tolerance, which is BC-ERR-10027; a later simplification slip costs this comparison alone.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorial or the power in the bound cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10002, or the inequality cannot be resolved, which is BC-PRQ-10001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10018 (at most against equals) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (evaluating the bound) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the assembled bound and a tolerance, evaluate the bound and present the inequality stating that the error is at most the bound and that the bound is at most the tolerance.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10017 (an error bound applied as a formula with no hypotheses)
BC-MIS-10018 (the bound written as the exact error)
BC-SKL-10039 (confirming the alternating conditions)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10009 (the Lagrange route, where a derivative bound is supplied)
BC-QA-10008 (the alternating route, where the omitted term is the bound)

BC-ERR-10033 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A bound is chosen and used cleanly while the reason for choosing it is not stated, or the Lagrange bound is reached for where the series alternates and no derivative bound is available, which is BC-ERR-10033.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The form of the series at the input cannot be read, so neither set of conditions can be checked, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10017 (the hypotheses each bound requires) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10039 (checking the alternating conditions) for the procedural case
