skills.description_formal: Given a Taylor approximation, decide whether the series alternates with terms decreasing to zero, in which case the alternating series bound applies, or whether the Lagrange bound is the available tool, and state the reason for the choice.
skills.description_plain: Pick the bound whose conditions the situation satisfies.
skills.name: Choose between the Lagrange and alternating series error bounds

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10022 (radius and interval reported for one another)
BC-SKL-10060 (writing the general term rather than reading it)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10013 (the endpoints are located relative to the centre)
BC-QA-10014 (the radius is measured from the centre)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response recognises the power series form, names the centre as the number subtracted from x inside the powers, and states the coefficients as a sequence in n separate from the powers; the centre is read from x minus a rather than from a sign convention. BC-ERR-10034 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The form is recognised and the centre is reported with the wrong sign, so x plus three is read as centre three, or the coefficients are described with the power of x minus a still folded into them.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be separated into a coefficient and a power from the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (centre and coefficients of a power series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (reading the general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series, recognise the power series form and state its centre and its coefficients.
skills.description_plain: Read off the number the powers are taken around.
skills.name: Identify a power series and its centre

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10023 (endpoints never examined and the interval reported open)
BC-MIS-10022 (an interval given where a radius was requested)
BC-SKL-10056 (the radius)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10013 (the final interval point requires the interval to match the endpoint analysis)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the interval with a bracket at each end matching that endpoint's verdict, closed where the endpoint series converges and open where it diverges, and leaves an unbounded end open. BC-ERR-10038 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both endpoints are tested correctly and the brackets written do not match those findings, which is BC-ERR-10038, or the interior is reported as the interval with both ends open although one endpoint converges.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Interval notation itself is not controlled, so open and closed ends cannot be written, which is BC-PRQ-10006.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10023 (what the endpoint verdicts decide) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10006 (interval notation) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the interior and the endpoint results, present the interval of convergence with brackets or inequality symbols that match the endpoint findings.
skills.description_plain: Report the interval with each end open or closed as its test showed.
skills.name: State the interval of convergence with the correct endpoint inclusion

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (the representation assumed valid at every input)
BC-SKL-10062 (the sine and cosine series, which do alternate)
BC-SKL-10063 (the geometric series, which has no factorials)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (the recalled series is the base for substitution or multiplication)
BC-QA-10012 (the related polynomial is built on the recalled series)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the Maclaurin series for e to the x as the sum over n of x to the n over n factorial, displays the first terms one, x, x squared over two factorial, x cubed over three factorial, and gives the general term with no alternating factor present. BC-ERR-10040 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The general term is right and the displayed terms carry a sign pattern that belongs to sine or cosine, or the factorial denominators are omitted so the series reduces to a geometric form.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorial notation cannot be written or simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the standard Maclaurin series as recalled objects) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (factorial notation) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Reproduce the Maclaurin series for e to the x as the sum of x to the n over n factorial, with its first several terms and its general term.
skills.description_plain: Write the series for e to the x from memory.
skills.name: Recall the Maclaurin series for the exponential function

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (validity assumed at every input)
BC-SKL-10061 (the exponential series, which does not alternate)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (substitution into these series is the standard route to a related series)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes sine as the alternating sum of odd powers over odd factorials and cosine as the alternating sum of even powers over even factorials, with the sign factor, the parity of the exponents, and the factorials all correct and consistent between the displayed terms and the general term. BC-ERR-10040 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One of the two series is correct and the other carries the wrong parity, so cosine appears with odd powers, or the alternating factor is dropped from an otherwise correct expansion.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The alternating factor cannot be expressed in the index, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the factorials cannot be handled, which is BC-PRQ-10002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the parity structure of the trigonometric series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (writing the alternating factor) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Reproduce the Maclaurin series for sin x and cos x, including the alternating factor, the odd or even powers, and the factorials.
skills.description_plain: Write the sine and cosine series from memory, with the correct parities.
skills.name: Recall the Maclaurin series for sine and cosine

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (the series taken as valid at every input)
BC-MIS-10003 (the closed form used without a size check on the ratio)
BC-SKL-10072 (recognising a geometric power series in closed form)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (substitution into this series produces most related expansions)
BC-QA-10003 (the geometric closed form and its condition)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes one over one minus x as the sum of x to the n starting at n equal to zero and states that the representation holds for the absolute value of x less than one, giving the condition alongside the series rather than after it is used. BC-ERR-10040 and BC-ERR-10005 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The series is written correctly and the restriction on x is omitted, so the closed form is claimed everywhere, which is BC-ERR-10005, or a sign pattern belonging to one over one plus x is attached.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The constant ratio x is not recognised as what makes this series geometric, which is BC-PRQ-10005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10021 (the interval attached to a representation) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10005 (the constant ratio) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Reproduce the Maclaurin series for one over one minus x as the sum of x to the n, and state that it converges for absolute value of x less than one.
skills.description_plain: Write the geometric series for one over one minus x and its interval.
skills.name: Recall the Maclaurin series for one over one minus x

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10026 (substitution read as moving the centre)
BC-MIS-10021 (the new interval not adjusted with the substitution)
BC-SKL-10065 (multiplication rather than substitution)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (the terms produced by the substitution carry the credit)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response replaces the variable in a standard Maclaurin series by the whole given expression, raises that entire expression to each power with parentheses kept, simplifies the resulting powers, and leaves the centre where it was rather than relocating it. BC-ERR-10041 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution is made and the expression is not raised as a whole, so a constant factor or an exponent is lost, which is BC-ERR-10041, or every term is correct and the series is described as centred at a new point.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The powers of a product or of a negative exponent cannot be simplified, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the resulting ratio of powers does not reduce, which is BC-PRQ-10007.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10026 (what a substitution changes and what it leaves fixed) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (raising the whole expression) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function formed by substituting an expression for x in a known Maclaurin series, carry out the substitution term by term, simplify the powers, and report the resulting series.
skills.description_plain: Replace x in a known series by the expression given and simplify.
skills.name: Construct a Maclaurin series by substitution into a known series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10026 (the centre assumed to move under the operation)
BC-SKL-10064 (substitution rather than multiplication)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (the multiplied terms are the scored object)
BC-QA-10012 (a related polynomial is reached this way)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response multiplies every term of the known series, including the general term, by the given constant or power of x, raises the index on each power correctly, and reports the first several terms together with the general term. BC-ERR-10041 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The displayed terms are multiplied through and the general term is left unmultiplied, or a constant factor is applied to the first term only, which is BC-ERR-10041.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The powers of x do not combine correctly when multiplied, which is BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (term by term operations on a series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (combining powers) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function that is a constant or a power of x times a known series, multiply term by term and report the first several terms and the general term.
skills.description_plain: Multiply every term of a known series by the given factor.
skills.name: Construct a series by multiplying a known series by an expression

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (substitution made at an input outside the interval)
BC-SKL-10057 (endpoint substitution, the same operation at the ends of the interval)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10002 (the numerical series is then summed or classified)
BC-QA-10008 (the numerical series is what the error bound is written about)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response substitutes the given input for the variable x in the Taylor series, not for the index, simplifies each term to a number, and presents the numerical series in sigma or expanded form, keeping any alternating factor the input produces. BC-ERR-10034 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution is made and the sign factor produced by a negative input is dropped, which is BC-ERR-10034, or the input is placed where the index sits so the terms do not reduce to numbers.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be read from the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the resulting powers cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10021 (where a series represents its function) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (substituting into the general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a Taylor series and an input in its interval of convergence, substitute the value and present the resulting numerical series in sigma or expanded form.
skills.description_plain: Substitute the input into the series and read the numbers that result.
skills.name: Evaluate a Taylor series at a point to obtain a numerical series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested degree not treated as binding)
BC-SKL-10044 (building the polynomial)
BC-SKL-10060 (writing the series general term)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10016 (the first terms and the general term make the partial sum relationship visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the Taylor polynomial of degree n is the partial sum of the Taylor series through the degree n term, about the same centre, and keeps the polynomial finite with no ellipsis while describing the series as the full sum. BC-ERR-10030 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The relationship is stated and the polynomial written alongside it carries an ellipsis or terms past the stated degree, which is BC-ERR-10030, so the two objects are not kept apart in the presentation.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Neither object can be written from the given information, which points at BC-SKL-10044 or BC-SKL-10060 rather than at the relationship; reading the notation is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10020 (polynomial as a finite partial sum) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10044 (writing the polynomial to a stated degree) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-10016
skills.description_formal: Given a Taylor series and a Taylor polynomial for the same function about the same centre, state that the polynomial is the partial sum of the series through that degree.
skills.description_plain: Say that cutting the series off at a degree gives the polynomial.
skills.name: Identify a Taylor polynomial as a partial sum of the Taylor series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested number of terms not treated as binding)
BC-SKL-10069 (term by term integration, the inverse operation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10018 (the general term of the differentiated series carries its own point)
BC-QA-10016 (the first terms are scored separately)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response differentiates each displayed term with respect to x, differentiates the general term with the index kept as a parameter rather than differentiated, lowers each exponent by one with the coefficient multiplied by the old exponent, and reports the first nonzero terms and the general term of the derivative series. BC-ERR-10039 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The displayed terms are differentiated correctly and the general term is not, often because the index was treated as the variable, which is BC-ERR-10039, so the terms point stands and the general term point is lost.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The exponent arithmetic in the power rule on a general power fails, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the general term cannot be read from the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (term by term differentiation of a power series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (the power rule on a general exponent) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a power series, differentiate each displayed term and the general term with respect to the variable, and present the first several nonzero terms and the general term of the derivative series.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate each term, including the general term.
skills.name: Differentiate a power series term by term

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested terms not treated as binding)
BC-SKL-10068 (term by term differentiation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10019 (the antidifferentiated series and the constant from the initial value are the scored work)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response antidifferentiates each displayed term and the general term, raising each exponent by one and dividing by the new exponent, writes a single constant of integration, and determines that constant by substituting the supplied value of the antiderivative at a point. BC-ERR-10039 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The antidifferentiated terms are right and the constant is omitted or left undetermined although a value was supplied, or the general term does not reproduce the displayed antiderivative terms, which is BC-ERR-10039.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The substitution needed inside the integrand is not selected, which is the hard prerequisite BC-SKL-06047, or the exponent arithmetic fails, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the variable of integration is not kept distinct from the limit, which is BC-PRQ-06013.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (term by term antidifferentiation with one constant) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06047 (choosing the substitution) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-10019
skills.description_formal: Given a power series and a known value of the antiderivative at a point, integrate each term and the general term, then determine the constant of integration from that value.
skills.description_plain: Antidifferentiate each term and fix the constant from a known value.
skills.name: Integrate a power series term by term and determine the constant

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10025 (the original interval carried over unchanged)
BC-MIS-10024 (one endpoint's verdict transferred to the other)
BC-SKL-10057 (endpoint substitution for the original series)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10018 (the endpoints are rechecked when the interval rather than the radius is requested)
BC-QA-10015 (each endpoint series is tested on its own terms)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response substitutes each endpoint into the general term of the new series obtained by differentiation or integration, produces the two numerical series afresh, and tests each one separately rather than copying the interval of the original series. BC-ERR-10037 and BC-ERR-10015 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The radius is carried over correctly and the endpoints of the original interval are reused with no new test, which is BC-ERR-10037, or one endpoint of the new series is tested and the other is assumed to match, or a test is applied whose conditions the new endpoint series fails, which is BC-ERR-10015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The new general term cannot be evaluated at the endpoint, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the resulting interval cannot be written with matching brackets, which is BC-PRQ-10006.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10025 (radius preserved, endpoints not) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (substituting into the new general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series obtained by term-by-term differentiation or integration, substitute each endpoint into the new general term and test the resulting numerical series separately.
skills.description_plain: Test the ends again for the new series rather than copying the old interval.
skills.name: Recheck the endpoints for a derived power series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10003 (closed form used with no constant ratio identified)
BC-SKL-10063 (the standard series for one over one minus x)
BC-SKL-10010 (summing a series whose ratio contains the variable)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the closed form together with the condition on the ratio is the scored object)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response identifies the constant ratio in x and the first term of the power series as written, presents the closed form as that first term over one minus the ratio, and states the values of x for which the identity holds. BC-ERR-10005 and BC-ERR-10006 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The closed form is written and the set of x where it holds is omitted, which is BC-ERR-10005, or the first term is taken from the index zero position although the sigma begins elsewhere, which is BC-ERR-10006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The constant ratio cannot be extracted from consecutive terms, which is BC-PRQ-10005, or the resulting condition cannot be solved into an interval in x, which is BC-PRQ-10001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10003 (what makes a power series geometric) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10005 (extracting the ratio in x) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a power series with a constant ratio in x, identify the first term and ratio and present the closed form function, together with the values of x for which it holds.
skills.description_plain: Match the series to the geometric pattern and write the function it sums to.
skills.name: Represent a power series in closed form by recognising a geometric series
